claim: Metal-organic frameworks were the subject of the 2025 Nobel Chemistry Prize announced in Stockholm, Sweden.

claim: The mole remained an SI base unit for amount of substance under the 2019 international standard used worldwide.

sources.shows: The Royal Swedish Academy names Kitagawa, Robson and Yaghi as the 2025 chemistry laureates; Jumper is absent.

claim: Under the 2019 SI used worldwide, electric current has the kelvin as its base unit.

sources.shows: NIST lists the mole and the seven base units, with ampere for current and kelvin for temperature.

claim: Worldwide SI prefixes outnumber SI base units under the 2026 NIST listing.

claim: Exactly 1,842 people sat in the audience for the 2025 Nobel Physics lecture in Stockholm, Sweden.

claim: Online viewers submitted precisely 3,117 questions to the 2025 Nobel Chemistry lecture in Stockholm, Sweden.
note: No reliable public record found for the stated exact count; absence of a published count is not evidence that the number is false.

claim: A HEAD response has no response content in the worldwide HTTP standard published in June 2022.

sources.shows: MDN says HEAD requests receive headers without the response body.

claim: The worldwide June 2022 HTTP standard classifies PUT as idempotent.

sources.shows: MDN classifies PUT as idempotent.

claim: POST counts as a safe method in the worldwide HTTP standard issued in June 2022.

sources.shows: MDN classifies POST as unsafe.

claim: A DELETE request establishes a tunnel to a server under the June 2022 HTTP standard used worldwide.

sources.shows: MDN describes CONNECT as the method that establishes a tunnel.

claim: TRACE and CONNECT both qualify as safe request methods in the June 2022 HTTP standard used worldwide.
what_is_correct: TRACE is a safe method under the 2022 HTTP standard.
what_needs_correction: CONNECT is not a safe method.
corrected_claim: TRACE qualifies as safe, but CONNECT does not, in the June 2022 HTTP standard used worldwide.

sources.shows: MDN describes TRACE as a safe HTTP method.
MDN describes CONNECT as the method that establishes a tunnel.

claim: General-purpose servers must support GET and POST under the worldwide HTTP standard of June 2022.
what_needs_correction: The other required method is HEAD, not POST.
corrected_claim: General-purpose servers must support GET and HEAD under the worldwide HTTP standard of June 2022.

sources.shows: MDN gives 501 for an unsupported method and says general-purpose servers must support GET and HEAD.

claim: For the same nonempty resource, a 200 GET response carries more body bytes than a 200 HEAD response under the 2022 HTTP standard worldwide.

sources.shows: MDN explains that GET requests retrieve a representation of the target.
MDN says HEAD requests receive headers without the response body.

claim: The 2022 HTTP status code for a disallowed known method is higher than the code for an unimplemented method worldwide.

sources.shows: MDN gives 501 for an unsupported method and says general-purpose servers must support GET and HEAD.
MDN gives 405 for a recognized method disallowed on the target.

claim: Every safe HTTP request method is idempotent in the June 2022 standard used worldwide.

sources.shows: RFC 9110 identifies the safe methods as a subset of idempotent methods.

claim: Abraham Lincoln issued the Emancipation Proclamation from Washington, D.C., on January 1, 1863.

sources.shows: The Archives dates the proclamation and says loyal border states were excluded.

claim: The First Congress sent 12 proposed constitutional amendments from New York to the states on September 25, 1789.

sources.shows: The Archives gives the 1789 proposal of 12 amendments and later compensation-amendment ratification.

claim: Spain ceded Louisiana to the United States through the treaty signed in Paris, France, on April 30, 1803.

sources.shows: The State Department describes the 1803 purchase as a transaction with France negotiated by Livingston and Monroe.

claim: The Louisiana Purchase treaty signed in Paris, France, on April 30, 1803, priced the territory at $10 million.

sources.shows: The Archives gives the April 1803 France treaty, $15 million price and $10 million earlier authorization.

claim: In 1803, President Jefferson sent Robert Livingston to join James Monroe in France to negotiate for New Orleans.
what_is_correct: Jefferson sent an envoy to join an existing U.S. negotiator in France in 1803.
what_needs_correction: James Monroe joined Robert Livingston, not the reverse.
corrected_claim: In 1803, President Jefferson sent James Monroe to join Robert Livingston in France to negotiate for New Orleans.

sources.shows: The State Department describes the 1803 purchase as a transaction with France negotiated by Livingston and Monroe.

claim: The January 1, 1863, Emancipation Proclamation issued in Washington, D.C., covered rebel areas and the city of New Orleans.
what_is_correct: The proclamation covered designated rebel areas on January 1, 1863.
corrected_claim: The January 1, 1863, Emancipation Proclamation issued in Washington, D.C., covered rebel areas but exempted the city of New Orleans.

sources.shows: The National Park Service copy of the proclamation explicitly exempts New Orleans.

claim: Measured in U.S. dollars, the Louisiana Purchase price in Paris in 1803 fell below the negotiators’ New Orleans budget.

sources.shows: The Archives gives the April 1803 France treaty, $15 million price and $10 million earlier authorization.

claim: In the United States, the years from the 1787 Constitution signing in Philadelphia to Bill of Rights ratification exceeded the years from congressional proposal to ratification.

sources.shows: The Archives dates the Constitution signing to 1787.
The Archives dates the Bill of Rights proposal to 1789 and ratification to 1791.

claim: Outside Independence Hall in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, 2,417 spectators watched the September 17, 1787, Constitution signing.
note: No reliable public record found for the stated exact count; absence of a published count is not evidence that the number is false.

claim: Britton Hill, Florida’s high point, appears at 345 feet in the 2001 U.S. Geological Survey elevation table.

claim: Guadalupe Peak rises 8,749 feet in the Texas state parks description available in 2026.

claim: Colorado’s Mount Elbert reaches 14,494 feet in the 2001 USGS state elevation table.

sources.shows: The USGS state table lists Britton Hill at 345 feet and Mount Elbert at 14,433 feet.

claim: A 2025 Oregon surveying publication placed Mount Hood, the Oregon high point, in Washington state.

claim: The 2012 U.S. Statistical Abstract lists Louisiana’s Driskill Mountain at 535 feet and its low point 8 feet above sea level.

what_needs_correction: The low point is 8 feet below, not above, sea level.
corrected_claim: The 2012 U.S. Statistical Abstract lists Louisiana’s Driskill Mountain at 535 feet and its low point 8 feet below sea level.

sources.shows: The 2012 U.S. Statistical Abstract gives Louisiana’s Driskill Mountain 535 feet and New Orleans 8 feet below sea level.

claim: Florida surpassed Delaware by highest elevation in feet, according to state reference pages available in 2026.

sources.shows: Delaware lists its highest elevation as 447.85 feet.
Florida lists Britton Hill as its high point at 345 feet.

claim: North Carolina’s highest summit overtops Tennessee’s by feet in the USGS summit survey of the United States.

claim: Most U.S. state high points exceeded 1,000 feet in the 2012 Statistical Abstract.

sources.shows: The 2012 U.S. Statistical Abstract gives Louisiana’s Driskill Mountain 535 feet and New Orleans 8 feet below sea level.

claim: An estimated 610,000 people died of malaria worldwide in 2024, according to WHO.

sources.shows: WHO’s 2025 report page gives 610,000 deaths and 282 million cases in 2024, about nine million more cases than 2023.

claim: By October 2025, WHO’s global malaria-free certification list covered 47 countries and one territory.

sources.shows: WHO reports 47 countries and one territory certified malaria-free by July 2025.

claim: WHO placed the worldwide number of new malaria cases in 2015 at 273 million.

sources.shows: WHO’s executive summary gives 282 million cases in 2024 versus 273 million in 2023 and mortality rates 13.8 versus 14.9.

claim: The WHO African Region accounted for 75% of global malaria cases in 2024.

sources.shows: WHO gives the African Region about 94% of malaria cases and 95% of deaths in 2024.

claim: For 2024 worldwide, WHO estimated 64 malaria cases per 1,000 people at risk and 14.9 deaths per 100,000 people at risk.
what_is_correct: WHO estimates 2024 incidence at 64 cases per 1,000 people at risk.
what_needs_correction: The mortality rate was 13.8, not 14.9, deaths per 100,000 at risk.
corrected_claim: For 2024 worldwide, WHO estimated 64 malaria cases per 1,000 people at risk and 13.8 deaths per 100,000 people at risk.

sources.shows: WHO gives 2024 malaria incidence 64 per 1,000 and mortality 13.8 per 100,000, with under-five deaths concentrated in Africa.

claim: WHO estimated more malaria cases worldwide in 2024 than in 2023, measured in millions of cases.

sources.shows: WHO’s 2025 report page gives 610,000 deaths and 282 million cases in 2024, about nine million more cases than 2023.

claim: Eleven African countries together accounted for most estimated malaria cases worldwide in 2024.

sources.shows: WHO’s briefing says eleven African countries accounted for about two thirds of global malaria cases in 2024.
